title: Israel, Jordan and Egypt sent planes and helicopters to fight the deadly wildfire in Cyprus

trailer.text: According to Devdiscourse, Jordan, Egypt, Israel, Spain and Greece swiftly dispatched aircraft and personnel to Cyprus, in a joint international effort against the fire.
On 23 July 2025, during a severe heatwave, a fire broke out near the village of Malia in the Limassol district, and it claimed the lives of two people.
According to the government spokesman, four Jordanian aircraft and two Egyptian helicopters were already on the island, and two planes from Israel were due to arrive.
Two Israeli C-130 aircraft were to make water drops at night.
Until sunset, a total of 13 firefighting aircraft made water drops.

paragraphs.text: That Wednesday, the temperature in Cyprus reached 43 degrees, and an amber weather alert was issued.
Cyprus has been suffering from a protracted drought, which has brought water resources down to very low levels.
According to the government spokesman, very strong winds, heat and extreme dryness after three winters with little rain created a "perfect storm".
The Ministry of Interior ordered immediate evacuations along a 14 km stretch of mountainous area.
According to AP, on Wednesday the fire forced the evacuation of at least 14 villages.
The two dead, an elderly couple, were found in a burned-out car on the road between the villages of Monagri and Alassa.
Police were still trying to identify their remains.
In the village of Lofou, at least 20 homes were destroyed, as the fire threatened a group of stranded evacuees trying to flee.
A rescue operation by the police and the National Guard for 36 residents of Lofou did not succeed.
According to the village head, the residents travelled in a police minibus, encountered a wall of fire and were forced to turn back to Lofou.
An electricity company substation in the area was completely destroyed, and at dawn on Thursday 15 villages were without electricity.
Cypriot President Christodoulides said there had never been anything like this in Cyprus.
According to the government spokesman, more than 250 firefighters, 75 fire engines and 14 aircraft were working to contain the flames.
Alongside the fire department, the forestry department, Civil Defence and the Limassol district local government authority were operating, assisted by organised groups and volunteers.
Private companies provided fuel for the aircraft free of charge, as well as other supplies for fighting the fire.
The President visited the command centre in Ayios Efraim, and called on residents to follow evacuation instructions.
He said the situation was very difficult, the fire front was huge and all forces had been mobilised.
According to the European Commission, Cyprus requested firefighting assistance through the EU Civil Protection Mechanism.
According to AP, aircraft from Jordan, Israel, Lebanon and Spain were on their way on Thursday.
According to the government spokesman, four Jordanian aircraft and two Egyptian helicopters were already on the island.
Egyptian Petroleum Minister Karim Badawi, who was visiting Cyprus, said that two specialised helicopters would arrive, to show that his country is a strategic and reliable partner.
According to Al Jazeera, a British Chinook helicopter based in Cyprus also assisted.
According to Devdiscourse, Jordan, Egypt, Israel, Spain and Greece swiftly sent aircraft and personnel in a joint international effort.
Until sunset, 13 firefighting aircraft made water drops.

stations.title: The planes from Israel fly at night

paragraphs.text: According to Anadolu, Israel confirmed it would provide aerial assistance under the direction of Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, and the aircraft were scheduled to depart on Thursday evening.
According to the Cypriot government spokesman, two planes from Israel were due to arrive.
These were two C-130 aircraft, which were to make water drops at night.
According to Christodoulides, the Israeli planes could also be used at night.

stations.title: After the fire: evacuees and rebuilding

paragraphs.text: According to Justice Minister Hartsiotis, evacuees from the affected communities were housed in temporary shelters.
Cyprus Red Cross volunteers distributed basic necessities in Ayios Ambrosios, Pachna, Trimikli and Episkopi.
The government pledged immediate financial support to community councils, full restoration of property damage, temporary housing and basic necessities.
Christodoulides promised help to people who lost their livelihood, and to property owners to rebuild their homes.
Antonis Christou, 67, from the village of Kantou, said he cried because the world was on fire.
Some locals accused the authorities of a slow response.
The head of the village of Souni-Zanakia said fire engines began arriving when the fire had already burned half the village.
According to Al Jazeera, residents vented their anger at what they called a disorganised response.
The government spokesman rejected the criticism, saying that fire crews had responded quickly and that all firefighting protocols had been activated from the start.
The Justice Minister said everything possible under the circumstances had been done and that this was not the time to assign blame.
According to Anadolu, Greece also faced criticism for a delayed response.
The Justice Minister explained that fires in Greece limited its ability to assist.
